correctness.rationale: For the specified action, a fixed open cell is an equivariant assignment of colors to unused or source slots, with all source slots hit. A target L-cycle has one unused choice or exactly ℓ phases for a receiving source ℓ-cycle dividing L. On each fixed relative interior there is one positive coordinate t_C per used target cycle and, for each source cycle of length ℓ, one independent equation ∑_{C assigned to it} (L_C/ℓ)t_C=1. Hence this stratum is nonempty with dimension t−r for t used target cycles and r source cycles. Its compactly supported Euler contribution is (−1)^(t−r). Inclusion–exclusion imposes that every source cycle is hit; complementing the omitted-cycle subset gives precisely the alternating signs and product in Φ. Barycentric subdivision fixes simplices of its fixed subcomplex pointwise, so ordinary Lefschetz equals fixed-set Euler. Babson–Kozlov Proposition 4.5 gives positive top degree n−m and concentration; the trivial H_0 contributes 1, yielding (−1)^(n−m)(Φ−1). For diagonal m=3, the identity top trace is 2^n−3 and the nonidentity ordinary Lefschetz values are 2 and 3; the weighted top average is [2^n−3+7(−1)^(n−3)]/6 and is positive starting at n=4 (value 1). Rational quotient chains after subdivision compute coinvariants, which are exact by averaging, so no freeness is assumed and the other reduced groups vanish. The mixed and pure-source examples at (3,5) also evaluate to 2 and −1. Inspected the frozen finite signed-cell test as corroboration only, not the proof of the infinite-scope result.

value.rationale: A uniform simultaneous character for all these Hom complexes is a structural result: it determines arbitrary finite subgroup quotient Betti numbers and detects mixed traces invisible to either the identity rank or the target restriction. The diagonal example illustrates why the joint character matters; the example alone, once the formula is known, is not an independently valuable new claim. Exact overlap rules out originality, not the mathematical usefulness of the formula.
